faq_geral_1_answer: Vectora is a self-hosted AI agent with RAG, a native Context Graph, and multi-user web chat — it runs on your own computer or server, never in a Vectora cloud.
faq_geral_2_answer: You download and install Vectora (Windows, macOS, or Linux) — it's a native app, not a Docker image. Teams that need shared web chat usually run the Linux build on their own VPS; Docker is only used to spin up the optional infrastructure for 'complete' storage mode (Postgres+Qdrant+Redis), never for Vectora itself.
faq_geral_3_question: Do I need a GPU to run it?
faq_geral_3_answer: No. Vectora uses LLMs and embeddings via API (Google, Anthropic, OpenAI, Cohere, Voyage, OpenRouter) or local Ollama. For individual use, any recent laptop runs it fine; for a team VPS, 2 vCPUs and 4 GB RAM are already enough.
faq_instalacao_1_answer: Windows 10+, macOS 12+, and Linux (Ubuntu 20.04+/Debian 11+/Fedora 35+) — native installers for all three, with built-in auto-update.
faq_instalacao_2_question: How do I deploy on a server for my team?
faq_instalacao_2_answer: Any Linux VPS with 2+ vCPUs and 4+ GB RAM — AWS, GCP, Hetzner, DigitalOcean, or your provider of choice. It's the same Linux installer (.AppImage/.deb/.rpm), just running on a server instead of your desktop.
faq_instalacao_3_answer: Less than 5 minutes: download the installer for your system, open the app, and create your root account on first launch. 'Complete' storage mode (optional, for scaling beyond the default SQLite+LanceDB) is deployed via a separate docker-compose — that part does take a few extra minutes.
faq_planos_1_question: What's the difference between Free and Pro?
faq_planos_1_answer: Free is free forever and requires no account: operational CLI, Desktop, and unlimited RAG (via Cohere/Voyage/Ollama), all running on your machine. Pro (R$24/month) requires an account and adds what only makes sense for teams: multi-user web chat, unlimited member invites, SSO/SAML, scalable storage (Postgres/Qdrant/Redis), webhooks, and priority support.
faq_planos_2_question: Do I need to create an account to use Vectora?
faq_planos_2_answer: No, not for local/solo use. The Free plan works 100% without login. An account is only needed for Pro's team features.
faq_planos_3_answer: Yes. No minimum commitment. Cancel from the dashboard anytime — your account automatically reverts to the Free plan.
faq_seguranca_1_question: Is my data sent to Vectora?
faq_seguranca_1_answer: No. Everything stays on your server. Vectora has no access to your documents, conversations, or code.
faq_seguranca_2_question: Is Vectora LGPD and GDPR compliant?
faq_seguranca_2_answer: Yes. Since your data stays on your own infrastructure, you keep full control over compliance.
faq_seguranca_3_answer: On Free, it's local use with no login. For Pro (account required), Vectora's own authentication supports email/password and magic links.
faq_tecnico_1_answer: Google Gemini (default), Anthropic, OpenAI, Cohere, Ollama (local), OpenRouter (proxy with hundreds of models), and any OpenAI-API-compatible provider.
faq_tecnico_2_answer: Embeddings via Cohere, Voyage, Ollama, or OpenRouter (local or hosted), LanceDB as the default vector store with dense vector search and optional reranking (Cohere/Voyage). In Complete mode (self-hosted with Postgres + Qdrant), search becomes hybrid (dense + BM25).
faq_tecnico_3_question: Does Vectora expose a public API or MCP server?
faq_tecnico_3_answer: No. Vectora is a workspace with AI — you and the agent share the filesystem, terminal, git, and browser inside the product itself, with no public REST API or embedded MCP server.

page_features_desc: Everything Vectora does, end to end — agent engine, code, browser, models, and infrastructure.
features_context_graph_desc: Combines structural parsing via tree-sitter with semantic extraction by an LLM to build a real graph of your repository's symbols, imports, and calls — not a generic text index. Powers GraphRAG search (relevance by graph proximity, not just vector similarity) and impact analysis: before applying a change, the agent can ask "what else does this affect?" and get an answer grounded in the code's actual structure, not a guess.
features_terminal_desc: A real terminal inside the workbench, not a text box pretending to be one — commands actually run, with output streaming, multiple tabs per workspace, and persistent per-session history. The agent and the user share the same terminal: what one runs, the other sees.
features_git_desc: A full Git panel in the workbench: visual diffs, a browsable commit history, stash, worktrees, and branch comparison — no need to leave the chat and open a terminal just to run `git log`. The agent sees the same repository state you see on screen.
features_explorer_desc: A workspace file tree with inline editing, create/rename/delete, and direct integration with the agent's context — drag a file into the chat, or ask the agent to open and edit something, and both views (yours and its) stay in sync in real time.
features_browser_desc: A built-in browser with a full DevTools panel — Console, Network, and Elements — built on Playwright and the real Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP), not a simulation. The agent can navigate, click, fill forms, and read the DOM the same way you would by hand, with the same debugging data you'd see in Chrome.
features_sandbox_desc: Native execution isolation per platform: bwrap + seccomp + Landlock on Linux, WSL2 on Windows, Seatbelt on macOS, and Singularity/Apptainer as a portable alternative. Commands and scripts the agent runs execute confined — without unrestricted access to the rest of your system — without requiring Docker or a full VM.
features_native_engine_summary: A purpose-built imperative loop, no external orchestration framework.
features_native_engine_desc: Vectora's agent runs on a conversation engine built from scratch — an imperative loop that re-reads the session history on every turn, streams the model call, and executes tool calls, without relying on a compiled node graph or an external orchestration framework. Conversation state never lives only in memory: it's always re-read from persistent storage, so a session survives a backend restart without losing context.
features_souls_summary: A catalog of specialized subagents — code, research, review, testing, DevOps, and more —, all running on the same native engine.
features_souls_desc: The orchestrator dynamically delegates to one of 10 SOULs depending on the task: Coder (files/terminal/git), Search (web/RAG), Reviewer (reads diffs, never writes), Tester, DevOps (CI/infra), Writer/Docs, Data Analyst, Security Auditor, Browser QA, and Planner. The tool restriction per SOUL is real enforcement — a bind on the model's function-calling, not a prompt suggestion: a SOUL without write access can't change a file, no matter how insistently the request asks. All of them share the same native conversation engine and the same tool registry — behavior profiles on the same foundation, not separate products.
features_kanban_summary: Delegate background tasks with dependencies, priority, and review.
features_kanban_desc: A real Kanban board on top of the agent engine: create tasks, assign them to an agent profile, define dependencies between them (with cycle detection), and track progress live via SSE. Every background run has a heartbeat watchdog that proves the agent is still alive — if it stops beating, the task is released back to the queue instead of getting stuck forever. Optional review column, subtask progress rollup, and multiple boards per workspace.
features_rag_summary: Embeddings from multiple providers, vector indexing, and optional reranking.
features_rag_desc: Embeddings via Cohere, Voyage, Ollama (local), or OpenRouter, indexed in LanceDB. In Complete mode, search combines dense (vector) retrieval with BM25 (lexical) — covering both "find something similar to this" and "find the file that has exactly this word". An optional reranker reorders results before they reach the agent's context, prioritizing precision over raw recall.
features_ollama_summary: Local models show up in chat automatically, no manual setup.
features_ollama_desc: Vectora detects an Ollama instance running on your machine and registers the available models directly into the chat's model picker — no config file to edit, no app restart. Run a fully offline local model, with zero API cost, through the same flow you'd use a hosted model.
features_nine_router_summary: Use your Codex, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot, and other subscriptions right inside Vectora, no per-token billing.
features_nine_router_desc: 9Router is an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible proxy that reuses the OAuth login of subscriptions you already pay for — OpenAI Codex, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code, and more — exposing all of them behind a single endpoint. Point Vectora at that proxy's URL and key in settings, and those subscriptions' models show up right in the chat, with no separate per-token charge. It's the opposite of OpenRouter (aggregated catalog, pay-per-token): 9Router is about reusing what you already pay for elsewhere.
features_openrouter_summary: A catalog with hundreds of models, using your own API key.
features_openrouter_desc: Connect your OpenRouter key and get access to their entire aggregated model catalog — from dozens of different providers, in one place — without needing a separate account for each. You pay the provider directly, with no Vectora markup.
features_mcp_summary: Connect third-party MCP servers — Vectora never becomes a server.
features_mcp_desc: Vectora consumes external MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers as a client — a marketplace of ready-made connectors, plus the option to point at any MCP server of your own. Deliberately, Vectora never exposes itself as an MCP server: that would make RAG and its other tools reachable from outside the shared workspace, which is the product's real differentiator.
features_library_summary: Publish, search, and reuse curated skills, connectors, and memories.
features_library_desc: A publishing and discovery space: reusable skills (packaged prompts/behaviors), ready-to-install MCP connectors, and curated memory buckets the agent can consult. Every item shows clear provenance (official, verified, or community) — nothing gets installed blind.
features_native_media_summary: Embedded ffmpeg, local transcription, and YouTube video reading.
features_native_media_desc: Media processing without depending on any API provider: embedded ffmpeg/ffprobe analyze audio and video locally, and faster-whisper transcribes audio fully offline when you don't want to spend tokens on a remote call. YouTube videos (and any platform supported by yt-dlp) are read first via the public transcript — without downloading the whole video — with on-demand frame extraction only when the agent needs visual context for a specific moment.
features_desktop_summary: Windows, macOS, and Linux — Electron over a compiled backend.
features_desktop_desc: A real desktop app on Windows, macOS, and Linux, with an Electron frontend talking to a Python backend compiled via Nuitka — never distributed source code, never trivially decompilable. In desktop mode, communication between the two layers is over a local named pipe / unix socket, never TCP: no port is opened on your machine.
features_web_multiuser_summary: The same Vectora, hosted, with accounts and role-based permissions.
features_web_multiuser_desc: Beyond desktop, Vectora runs as a multi-user web server (Pro plan) — multiple people, each with their own authentication, accessing the same instance with role-based permission control (root/admin/member/viewer). Safe folders and tool policies configurable by an administrator.
features_i18n_summary: Full interface in Portuguese, English, Spanish, and 4 more languages.
features_i18n_desc: The entire interface — chat, settings, onboarding — is translated into 7 languages: Portuguese, English, Spanish, French, Italian, German, and Russian. No hardcoded strings: every visible piece of text goes through a central message system, so adding a new language doesn't require hunting for strings scattered across the code.
features_services_summary: The Cloudflare Worker that powers the infrastructure behind Vectora.
features_services_desc: A Cloudflare Worker responsible for much of what connects Vectora to the world outside your computer: it hosts the install binaries for every version, notifies outdated apps and delivers the update itself, acts as the relay for Vectora Connect (the fixed URL bot platforms require), serves the site's issues page — where anyone can post requests, like a GitHub board — and backs the Pro plan's user accounts (no account is needed to use Vectora locally for free) and their admin panel.
features_vps_summary: Run Vectora on your own server, always online — not just on your computer.
features_vps_desc: Beyond the desktop app and the local multi-user web mode, the Pro plan lets you host Vectora on your own VPS: the instance stays always available, without depending on your computer being on, with the same agent engine and the same features as desktop.
features_connect_summary: Talk to Vectora through Telegram and other chat platforms.
features_connect_desc: Vectora bots available on several messaging platforms — Telegram is the first, with more to come — so you can talk to your agent without opening the app. Each bot is activated from the Vectora Pro panel; Vectora Services acts as the relay, providing the fixed URL each platform requires.
features_storage_avancado_summary: PostgreSQL, Qdrant and Redis instead of the default embedded storage.
features_storage_avancado_desc: By default, Vectora already runs on embedded storage — SQLite, LanceDB and NATS — with no external dependency to install. Advanced Storage swaps that base for PostgreSQL, Qdrant and Redis, built for heavier load and multiple simultaneous users; that's why it's a Pro plan feature.
features_bot_gha_summary: Automatic pull request review, right in your CI.
features_bot_gha_desc: Vectora itself running inside your repository's GitHub Actions: when a pull request opens, the bot reviews the changes and comments automatically, using whichever model provider you configure (9Router, OpenRouter, Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic and others). Set up through a dedicated panel, no manual YAML editing required.
